title: Scheduler readiness ordering must be code-point deterministic
description: Objective: remove a locale-dependent comparison from an ordering the determinism contract requires to be total and host-independent. Register item 9 of 11 from task-963cf1d125134c6193b7af0e53deeac3 (2026-08-14 product audit; verified real). Epic rail 4 applies: this is a determinism defect, so its fix must be pinned by exact codes, not by a passing sort. RE-MEASURED STILL OPEN at HEAD 192360e: packages/scheduler/src/readiness/readiness-projection.ts:152 tie-breaks with `String(a.edgeKey).localeCompare(String(b.edgeKey))`. localeCompare's result depends on the host ICU data and collation locale, so two hosts can order the same readiness set differently. THE REPO ALREADY AGREES THIS IS WRONG and provides the fix pattern in three other places: packages/import/src/canonical-bytes.ts:60 states 'localeCompare is not a stable total order - its result depends on the host's ICU'; packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/artifact-object-inventory.ts:168 and git-integration-inventory.ts:224 both say 'Code points, never localeCompare'; and recovery-inventory-shape.ts:41 documents the same. This is the one remaining production call site. Deliverable: replace it with a code-point comparison matching the landed convention. NOT in scope: changing the primary sort key, the readiness projection contract, or the other three modules that already comply. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: readiness-projection.ts:152 no longer calls localeCompare; the tie-break is a code-point comparison matching the convention already documented in packages/import/src/canonical-bytes.ts and the three runner recovery-inventory modules.
A repo-wide grep for localeCompare over production sources returns zero hits in packages/scheduler, and the grep is run with a positive control so a zero result is proven rather than assumed.
A test pins the exact resulting order for a set whose localeCompare order and code-point order DIFFER - a case where the two agree would pass before and after the fix and proves nothing.
The ordering is asserted to be a total order on the production surface: equal primary keys tie-break deterministically, and no two distinct entries compare equal.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test exits 0.
taskRails: The test MUST use inputs whose locale order and code-point order genuinely differ; otherwise it is green before the fix and the drill proves nothing.
Do not change the primary sort key or the projection's public ordering contract - this is a tie-break correctness fix only.
Follow the landed convention rather than inventing a fourth comparison helper; three modules already document the exact pattern.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source; split before 400.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED FIRST, and make the fixture prove itself. Add a test over the production reason-ordering path in packages/scheduler/src/readiness/ that pins the exact resulting order for reasons whose layer and code are EQUAL and whose edgeKey differs, using edgeKey values where locale collation and UTF-16 code-unit order genuinely DISAGREE - e.g. an uppercase/lowercase pair such as "B" and "a" (code units: "B" 0x42 sorts before "a" 0x61; most locale collations order "a" before "B"). CRITICAL, and this is the difference between a real test and a vacuous one: assert IN THE TEST that the two orders actually disagree on the host running it - compare `"a".localeCompare("B")` against the code-unit comparison and fail loudly if they agree. Without that guard, a host whose ICU collation happens to match code units makes the test pass BEFORE the fix and it certifies nothing. Confirm this test is RED against current bytes before touching production, and record that red.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED recorded, and red for the RIGHT reason rather than merely red.

RE-MEASURED BEFORE EDITING (the register's :152 is a snapshot). At HEAD 192360e, grep -rn localeCompare over packages/scheduler/src/ returns exactly ONE hit, still at readiness-projection.ts:152, inside the reasons comparator at :146-153. File is 240 physical lines by grep -c ''. The line above it at :151 already uses the locale-independent form, so the file disagrees with itself — evidence this was an oversight, not a choice.

THE RED:
  AssertionError: expected [ 'dev-edge-alpha', 'dev-edge-Beta' ] to deeply equal [ 'dev-edge-Beta', 'dev-edge-alpha' ]
Production returns COLLATION order (alpha before Beta); the test demands CODE-UNIT order ("B" 0x42 before "a" 0x61). That is the defect itself, not a fixture or wiring error.

THE DIVERGENCE GUARD PASSED IN THE SAME RUN — 1 failed | 1 passed. This is the part that decides whether the test is worth anything. localeCompare depends on host ICU data and default collation, so a fixture that diverges on my machine may not diverge in CI, and a non-divergent fixture passes BEFORE and after the fix. The guard asserts on the host actually running it that Math.sign("dev-edge-alpha".localeCompare("dev-edge-Beta")) differs from the code-unit comparison, and separately pins byCodeUnit(upper, lower) === -1 so the expected direction is stated rather than inferred. It went green, so the second test's red is a real measurement of divergent inputs. This is epic rail 4's "a generated or swept case must assert that the case was actually generated", applied to a hand-written fixture. Host resolved locale is en-US (Intl.Collator().resolvedOptions().locale).

DRIVEN THROUGH THE PRODUCTION SURFACE, not a re-implemented comparator. The comparator lives in collectReasons, which is NOT exported, so the test calls the exported projectReadiness and reads node.reasons. Global rail: a property must be asserted against the production surface, never a test helper that reimplements it. The local byCodeUnit helper in the test exists ONLY inside the divergence guard to characterise the fixture; no assertion about ordering is made against it.

THE FIXTURE COLLIDES ABOVE THE TIE-BREAK, which is what makes it a tie-break test. A self-contained graph (built inline in the test file, NOT added to the shared test-fixtures.ts, which other tasks may be editing) gives the completion node two UNSATISFIED incoming HARD edges. Both reasons are therefore layer LOGICAL and code HARD_DEPENDENCY_UNSATISFIED — asserted explicitly, so if a future change made them differ at a higher level the test would fail rather than silently stop testing the tie-break. Only edgeKey can decide the order.

FIXTURE LEGALITY CHECKED, not assumed: graph-key.ts:9 SAFE_GRAPH_KEY is /^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._:@/+~-]*$/u, so mixed-case edge keys are valid and the graph validates (asserted in tieGraph). A fixture rejected at an earlier layer would never reach the comparator.

Test file now 357 lines; production untouched this step (sha256 7de1363306dd54db47b636686b22880ed62b4256c5feea2576260fc5717ab070, unchanged).

implementationPlan.description: Fix the one line. packages/scheduler/src/readiness/readiness-projection.ts:152 currently ends the comparator with `return byCode !== 0 ? byCode : String(a.edgeKey).localeCompare(String(b.edgeKey));`. Replace the localeCompare tie-break with the same code-unit form the SAME comparator already uses one line above at :151 (`const byCode = a.code < b.code ? -1 : a.code > b.code ? 1 : 0;`) - so the two tie-break levels become consistent. Use the scheduler's OWN landed idiom, which already appears inline twice in this package: admission/admission-model.ts:165 and readiness/readiness-cursor.ts:60 both use `a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0`. Do NOT import byCodeUnit from @moe/import: its own doc comment declares it 'The ONLY string comparator this package may use', and pulling a three-line comparator across a package boundary would require a dependency edge for no benefit. Leave the READINESS_LAYERS primary ordering and the code-level tie-break untouched; this is a tie-break correctness fix only.

Prove the removal is complete rather than local. Run a grep for localeCompare across packages/scheduler production sources and require zero hits - and run it WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, per the standing rule that an empty grep proves nothing until the same query shape is shown to hit somewhere it must: run the identical grep over packages/import/src/canonical-bytes.ts and packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/, where the string appears in the doc comments that document this exact convention. Record both results. If any further localeCompare call site turns up in scheduler production code, fix it in this task and note it - the register recorded one site, but the register is a snapshot.

implementationPlan.description: Assert the ordering is a TOTAL order on the production surface, not merely that one pair now sorts correctly. Add a test that runs the production comparator over a set containing entries that collide on layer, entries that collide on layer AND code, and entries distinct at every level, and assert: the resulting order is exactly the expected sequence; sorting the same set from a different initial permutation yields the identical result (so the order does not depend on input order); and no two distinct entries compare equal. Assert an exact non-zero case count with a hand-written literal. This is what makes the fix a determinism guarantee rather than a single passing example.
implementationPlan.note:
Total-order tests landed: 26 passed (26), exit 0. THEN I DRILLED THEM AND FOUND THEY PROVE LESS THAN THE STEP ASSUMED. Recording that rather than shipping the stronger claim.

WHAT LANDED. One node carrying reasons at all three layers, covering the three required collision classes: distinct at every level (LOGICAL vs ADMISSION vs DISPATCH), colliding on layer only (HARD_DEPENDENCY_UNKNOWN vs HARD_DEPENDENCY_UNSATISFIED, both LOGICAL — "K" < "S" by code units), and colliding on layer AND code (three HARD_DEPENDENCY_UNSATISFIED differing only by edgeKey: dev-edge-Alpha 0x41, dev-edge-Beta 0x42, dev-edge-alpha 0x61). Exact expected sequence pinned as a hand-written literal. Permutation invariance over all 4! orderings of the edges plus a reversed fact order. Hand-written counts: expect(orders.length).toBe(24) and expect(expected.length).toBe(6), so a sweep that silently produced zero or one case cannot pass.

TWO MUTATION DRILLS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE FINDING.
DRILL 1 — restore `String(a.edgeKey).localeCompare(String(b.edgeKey))`: RED, 2 failed | 24 passed. Both the step-1 tie-break test and the new exact-sequence test fail. This is the regression that actually happened, and it is locked out.
DRILL 2 — replace the tie-break with `return 0`: GREEN. All 26 pass.

I DID NOT LEAVE DRILL 2 AS A SHRUG. I traced why, and the answer is in another module: frontier.ts:219-221 ALREADY sorts each blocked node's reasons by edgeKey, using the identical code-unit form `a.edgeKey < b.edgeKey ? -1 : a.edgeKey > b.edgeKey ? 1 : 0`. Array.prototype.sort is stable, so that canonical order survives this comparator's (layer, code) regrouping even when the edgeKey level does nothing. `return 0` is therefore an EQUIVALENT MUTANT through projectReadiness — not a hole in the test.

WHY THAT DOES NOT MAKE THE FIX POINTLESS, which is the obvious next question. `return 0` is inert; localeCompare is DESTRUCTIVE. It took an already-canonical upstream order and actively re-sorted it into host collation order — which is exactly what the step-1 red showed (production returned alpha, Beta; canonical is Beta, alpha). The defect was never a missing tie-break, it was a tie-break that corrupted a correct input in a host-dependent way.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DoD 4, stated plainly because QA will run this drill. The edgeKey tie-break's positive ordering contribution is NOT independently observable through the public surface: every path that produces reasons with a non-null edgeKey comes through frontier.ts pre-sorted, and predicate reasons all carry edgeKey null. So these tests prove (a) the projection is deterministic end to end under input permutation, and (b) reintroducing localeCompare reddens immediately. They do NOT prove the tie-break is what orders equal-key reasons, and I have written that into the test file's doc comment rather than letting a future reader infer the stronger claim.

I KEPT THE TIE-BREAK DELIBERATELY. Deleting it would make this comparator correct only by coupling to a sort two modules upstream plus an implicit reliance on sort stability. Task rail 2 also scopes this task to a tie-break correctness fix. The doc comment now warns against "simplifying" it away and says why the drill is green.

TESTS ADJUSTED TO MATCH WHAT THEY PROVE, not left overclaiming. The block's doc comment previously said permutation invariance witnesses totality "as a direct consequence"; that is false here, since upstream canonicalization plus stability would satisfy it regardless. It now states the measurement, names frontier.ts:219-221, and records the equivalent mutant explicitly. The set-size test is labelled as what it is — a fixture guard proving the six entries have distinct sort keys, so the permutation check is exercising keys that could have reordered.

FIXTURE LEGALITY, found the hard way: the first version put READINESS_CAPABILITY and READINESS_NO_PAUSE into the bundle while the all-true set still contained them, and the projection refused it as READINESS_INPUT_MALFORMED / "nodeFacts[4] is malformed" before any sorting happened. A duplicate-code bundle never reaches the comparator, so the test would have been measuring the wrong layer. Both codes are now removed before being re-added as CONFIRMED_FALSE, and the refusal is what proved the fixture had to be valid at the earlier layer first.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WHICH COMPARATOR TO USE. Importing byCodeUnit from @moe/import was rejected on two grounds: its own doc comment declares it 'The ONLY string comparator this package may use' (scoping it to @moe/import), and crossing a package boundary for a three-line comparator would require a real workspace dependency edge - manifest entry, lockfile importer, compiled probe - under the global dependency-edge rail, which is absurd overhead for `a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0`. Extracting a new shared comparator package was rejected for the same reason. CHOSEN: match the scheduler's own inline idiom, already present at admission-model.ts:165 and readiness-cursor.ts:60, which also makes the comparator internally consistent with its own :151.

THE TEST FIXTURE IS THE REAL RISK, NOT THE FIX. The fix is trivially correct; a test that fails to prove anything is the likely failure mode. A pair whose locale order and code-unit order happen to AGREE passes both before and after the change. Worse, whether they agree is host-dependent - which is the very property under test - so a fixture that is divergent on the author's machine can be non-divergent in CI and silently turn the test vacuous. CHOSEN: assert the divergence itself inside the test, so the fixture proves it is a real test case on the host actually running it. This is the epic rail's 'a generated or swept case must assert that the case was actually generated', applied to a hand-written fixture.

SCOPE HELD DELIBERATELY NARROW. The primary READINESS_LAYERS ordering and the code-level tie-break are untouched; widening to 'audit all scheduler ordering' would turn a one-line determinism fix into an open-ended sweep. Step 3 does run a scheduler-wide grep, but as a completeness CHECK with a positive control, not as licence to refactor.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 192360e (I also raised this slice from the audit register at the same HEAD, so the evidence below is first-hand, not inherited).

THE DEFECT IS ONE LINE, AND THE FILE ALREADY DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. packages/scheduler/src/readiness/readiness-projection.ts, comparator at :146-153:
  const byLayer = READINESS_LAYERS.indexOf(a.layer) - READINESS_LAYERS.indexOf(b.layer);
  if (byLayer !== 0) return byLayer;
  const byCode = a.code < b.code ? -1 : a.code > b.code ? 1 : 0;              // :151 CORRECT
  return byCode !== 0 ? byCode : String(a.edgeKey).localeCompare(String(b.edgeKey)); // :152 WRONG
The code-level tie-break one line above already uses the locale-independent form. Only the edgeKey tie-break reaches for localeCompare, which is strong evidence this is an oversight rather than a considered choice.

THE FIX PATTERN IS ALREADY LANDED IN THIS PACKAGE, TWICE, INLINE: packages/scheduler/src/admission/admission-model.ts:165 and packages/scheduler/src/readiness/readiness-cursor.ts:60 both use `a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0`. So the fix is to match the scheduler's own idiom, not to introduce anything new.

THE REPO-WIDE CONVENTION IS DOCUMENTED IN FOUR PLACES, which is why this is HIGH rather than cosmetic: packages/import/src/canonical-bytes.ts:57-64 defines byCodeUnit with the comment 'localeCompare is not a stable total order - its result depends on the host's ICU data, so two machines can order the same two paths differently and produce different canonical digests from identical bytes. That failure never reproduces locally.' packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/artifact-object-inventory.ts:168 and git-integration-inventory.ts:224 both carry 'Code points, never localeCompare'. recovery-inventory-shape.ts:41 documents the same.

planningNotes.risks:
A VACUOUS TEST IS THE MAIN HAZARD. localeCompare's behavior depends on host ICU data and the default collation locale. A fixture pair that diverges under en-US may not diverge under the C locale or a minimal-ICU Node build, and then the test passes before the fix and certifies nothing. The step-1 divergence guard is not optional garnish - it is the only thing that makes this test meaningful, and QA should check it exists.

CONFIRM RED BEFORE GREEN. Because the fix is one line, it is very easy to write the test and the fix together and never observe the red. Record the failing run explicitly; a test that was never red against current bytes has not been shown to test anything.

AN EMPTY GREP PROVES NOTHING ALONE. Step 3's zero-hit result must be paired with a positive control over files where localeCompare demonstrably appears (the import and runner doc comments), or a mistyped pattern reads as a clean sweep.

HOST-DEPENDENT BUGS DO NOT REPRODUCE LOCALLY. canonical-bytes.ts says this outright: 'That failure never reproduces locally.' Nobody should conclude the ordering was fine because the suite was green on one machine - greenness on a single host is exactly what this class of defect looks like.

LINE BUDGET: readiness-projection.ts is 240 of a 250 target. Replace the expression; do not add a local helper function to the file.

SHARED WORKTREE. Peers commit continuously and HEAD has moved repeatedly this session. Re-measure the line number before editing - :152 is a snapshot - and commit by explicit pathspec only.
